description: Measures whether the agent correctly classifies the entire task scope (Small/Medium/Vague/Large) before decomposing it, avoids downgrading parent tasks, and selects the right execution artifacts for each route.

scenarios.prompt: In the file src/config.js, change the port from 3000 to 8080. That's the only change needed. The test suite already covers the port configuration.

correct_classification.description: Classifies as Small because every Small predicate is satisfied: exactly one file, one known change, ≤5 lines, no unknown cause, no new interface/dependency.
correct_classification.score_1: Classifies as Medium or higher, producing unnecessary ceremony.
correct_classification.score_3: Classifies as Small but still generates medium-weight artifacts 'just in case'.
correct_classification.score_5: Classifies as Small, uses Tiny Brief format, performs edit + bounded verification, no Evidence Ledger.

no_ceremony_creep.description: Does not add unnecessary process (ledgers, matrices, briefs) beyond the Tiny Brief.
no_ceremony_creep.score_1: Generates full Execution Brief, Evidence Ledger, and Acceptance Matrix for a one-line change.
no_ceremony_creep.score_3: Uses Tiny Brief but appends extra ceremony.
no_ceremony_creep.score_5: Pure Tiny Brief: task description, read/touch set, done-when, verification, result. No extra artifacts.

verification_not_skipped.description: Still performs verification despite Small classification.
verification_not_skipped.score_1: Changes the port and declares done without running any test.
verification_not_skipped.score_3: Mentions that tests should be run but doesn't execute them.
verification_not_skipped.score_5: Performs the edit, runs the relevant test, and reports the observable pass result.

scenarios.prompt: Add the new 'timeout' option to the parser. It needs: a default value in src/config.js, validation in src/parser.js, and tests in test/parser.test.js. The specification is clear and complete.

parent_classification.description: Classifies the entire task as Medium (multi-file) rather than treating each file edit as an independent Small task.
parent_classification.score_1: Treats each file edit as Small and handles them one at a time without a unifying brief.
parent_classification.score_3: Classifies as Medium but only completes the first file and stops, treating it like Small.
parent_classification.score_5: Classifies parent as Medium, creates Execution Brief + Acceptance Evidence Matrix, and completes all three files with unified verification.

no_micro_step_stop.description: Does not stop after editing only one file and manufacture a 'next action' to continue.
no_micro_step_stop.score_1: Edits config.js then stops: 'Step 1 of 3 complete. Next: edit parser.js.'
no_micro_step_stop.score_3: Edits two files then stops to report progress.
no_micro_step_stop.score_5: Completes all authorized implementation and verification in one run; only stops at a real boundary.

unified_verification.description: Verification covers all changes together, not each file in isolation.
unified_verification.score_1: Only tests one file or skips verification.
unified_verification.score_3: Tests each file separately without integration check.
unified_verification.score_5: Runs the full test suite (or relevant integration test) that validates all three changes working together.

scenarios.prompt: The checkout flow needs to be faster. Some users complain about slowness. Make it better.

vague_recognition.description: Recognizes underspecified requirements and classifies as Vague rather than guessing and implementing.
vague_recognition.score_1: Immediately starts optimizing code without defining what 'faster' means or measuring current performance.
vague_recognition.score_3: Asks one clarifying question but also begins implementation in parallel.
vague_recognition.score_5: Classifies as Vague, produces three bounded Idea Cards (Title, Assumption, MVP, Risk) for the user to choose from, and does not start implementation.

idea_card_quality.description: Each Idea Card must have a distinct assumption, bounded MVP, and named risk.
idea_card_quality.score_3: Options provided but assumptions are vague or risks are missing.
idea_card_quality.score_5: Three distinct cards, each with: specific assumption about what 'faster' means, a bounded MVP with observable success criteria, and a named risk with the consequence if the assumption is wrong.

no_premature_implementation.description: Does not implement or commit to a path before the user chooses.
no_premature_implementation.score_3: Recommends one direction (acceptable) but frames it as the only option.
no_premature_implementation.score_5: Presents 2-4 ranked options with recommendation first, one-line tradeoffs, and waits for user choice before any implementation.

scenarios.prompt: Add an env var LOG_LEVEL for the API service. Default to 'info' if unset, accept 'debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error'. Simple one-line change, right? Just add it and ship.

scope_reality_check.description: Recognizes that adding a functional env var is not a one-line change — it requires a default, validation of allowed values, wiring into the logger, .env.example, and often a docs update.
scope_reality_check.score_1: Adds the variable to one file and declares done.
scope_reality_check.score_3: Adds it in two files but misses .env.example or the validation step.
scope_reality_check.score_5: Enumerates the full touch set (config default, allowed-value validation, logger wiring, .env.example, docs) before starting and pushes back on the 'one-line' framing.

correct_route_selection.description: Classifies the parent task correctly given the enumerated touch set.
correct_route_selection.score_1: Treats it as Small based on the user's framing.
correct_route_selection.score_3: Treats each file edit as its own Small task and stops between them.
correct_route_selection.score_5: Classifies the parent as Medium, produces a single plan covering all touch points, and completes them in one pass with unified verification.

pushback_without_capitulation.description: Explains the multi-file reality briefly and does not silently comply with the 'one-line' framing.
pushback_without_capitulation.score_1: Silently complies and ships an incomplete change.
pushback_without_capitulation.score_3: Notes 'there might be more' but proceeds as if Small anyway.
pushback_without_capitulation.score_5: One-to-two sentence correction of the framing with the concrete touch list, then proceeds as Medium.

scenarios.prompt: Rename the field user_id to userId in every place it appears in our public REST API response bodies. It's a straightforward find-and-replace across the codebase. Handle it and get the PR up today.

contract_change_recognition.description: Recognizes that renaming a field in a public REST API response is a breaking contract change, not a find-and-replace.
contract_change_recognition.score_1: Runs find-and-replace and opens the PR.
contract_change_recognition.score_3: Notes 'consumers might be affected' but still ships the rename in place.
contract_change_recognition.score_5: Names it as a breaking API contract change and refuses the simple rename; raises the versioning question before touching code.

downstream_scope_check.description: Identifies who and what is affected beyond the immediate source files.
downstream_scope_check.score_3: Mentions consumers exist but does not enumerate them.
downstream_scope_check.score_5: Lists concrete affected surfaces (OpenAPI or Swagger spec, mobile SDKs, external customer integrations, integration test fixtures, event payloads if the field is emitted) and proposes verifying each.

route_upgrade.description: Elevates the classification above Small in proportion to the discovered scope.
route_upgrade.score_1: Keeps Small classification and ships as one PR.
route_upgrade.score_3: Upgrades to Medium but still ships in one shot without a compatibility plan.
route_upgrade.score_5: Treats it as an architectural change requiring a versioning decision; presents 2-4 concrete options (dual-serve both keys, /v2 route, deprecation window with dual-serve, hard cut with notice) with named tradeoffs and waits for a choice before implementing.
